diagnosis.root_cause: EPON0/2 is down for the customers visible in the live port probe. All eight probed ONUs return definite offline answers (responds=true, online=0), while the OLT itself responds to ping and SNMP and the other tested PONs are healthy. The OLT health record also identifies a failed PON but incorrectly reports the overall status as healthy.
evidence: The live ONU probe gives definite offline results because each ONU responds but reports online=0; this is a real outage, not a monitoring timeout.
All eight ONUs visible on EPON0/2 are offline, so the failure is shared across the PON port rather than limited to customer 31035.
The OLT ping, SNMP, and OID subtree all respond, with normal CPU, memory, temperature, and uptime; therefore this is not an OLT-wide failure.
The other two tested PONs are marked healthy, further localizing the fault to EPON0/2.
The OLT population has 27 offline customers, which is close to the 24 customers assigned to EPON0/2 and far above the normal background level; this supports a port-scale outage.

Historical optical telemetry was stable and normal before the outage: RX was approximately -21 dBm, TX approximately +2.3 dBm, distance remained 157, and TX bias stayed healthy. There is no evidence of fibre, laser, distance, or authentication degradation causing the current outage.
The customer has a valid, CRM-consistent RADIUS entry, the expected VLAN 1082 is present, and the router is healthy, so provisioning, authentication, VLAN, and router faults are not indicated.
The overall OLT health label is contradictory because the detail identifies a failed PON; the genuine underlying service fault remains the PON port failure.

remediation.action: Escalate to access-network operations to inspect and restore EPON0/2, including the OLT port, uplink optics, patching, and associated splitter/feed. Verify all 24 customers on EPON0/2 after repair and confirm ONU registration and optical readings. Correct the OLT health-check aggregation so a failed PON cannot produce an overall healthy status.

ground_truth.root_cause: All 24 customers on EPON0/2 lost service within the same minute. The OLT is healthy and its other two ports are serving normally, so the fault is confined to this PON port: the port optics, the feeder fibre or the primary splitter.
expected_reasoning: The subject ONU is offline with responds true and online 0
Probing the rest of EPON0/2 shows every ONU returning the same definite offline answer
All of them stopped within the same minute, which rules out coincidence
OLT ping and SNMP succeed, uptime is 77 days, and CPU, memory and temperature are at baseline
The other two PON ports on this OLT are serving customers normally
The failure boundary follows the port exactly, so the fault is the port and not the OLT
Signal history on the subject was flat and healthy until the cut-off, so this is not progressive degradation
PON port traffic has collapsed from its usual level to near zero
A whole port failing at once points to port optics, the feeder or the primary splitter
distractors: The health check still reports the OLT healthy because two of three ports pass
A single-customer complaint would frame this as an individual fault
